title: A Bakery for the Summer
premise: Beatrix Okonkwo, once a celebrated cellist who walked off stage mid-concert and never went back, retreats to her late aunt's failing bakery in the coastal town of Merrow Point, planning one quiet summer of anonymity and sourdough. A freak June snowstorm traps her overnight in the shop with Elias Vane, the man she loved and abandoned at twenty-three, now a lawyer fighting to demolish the bakery's block for a development, and his rival Julian Marsh, a preservationist with his own claim on Beatrix's past. As the bakery becomes the town's battleground, Beatrix must testify about what really happened the night her career ended, choosing between the justice the law offers and the justice that costs more. She reclaims her music, her voice, and finally her whole heart, choosing Elias not because he is safe but because staying invisible no longer is.
about_author: S. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former orchestral librarian who spent a decade backstage before turning to fiction full-time. They write love stories set in kitchens, concert halls, and small towns that refuse to stay quiet.

chapters.title: The Last Note She Owed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A flashback-tinged opening: mid-concert, her bow arm fails, and she walks off the stage of her life. Emotional beat: shame crystallizing into a vow never to be seen again. She sells her cello and drives to Merrow Point.

chapters.title: Flour and Silence
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She inherits her aunt Rosa's bakery and discovers it's drowning in debt and a demolition notice. She tells herself she's only staying the summer. Emotional beat: grief disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: The Man at Table Three
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Elias Vane walks in for coffee, and the past walks in with him. Their charged, brittle exchange reveals they haven't spoken in nine years. Emotional beat: old love as a wound that never scarred.

chapters.title: Terms of the Demolition
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He's the development's lead counsel and didn't know Rosa's bakery was the property in question. Duty says proceed; memory says run. Emotional beat: the first crack in his professional armor.

chapters.title: A Rival with a Clipboard
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Julian Marsh arrives to survey the building for historical preservation, charming and persistent, clearly interested in more than the architecture. Emotional beat: the dangerous comfort of being admired from a safe distance.

chapters.title: What the Storm Brought In
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A freak June snowstorm kills the power and strands Elias and Julian in the bakery overnight. Forced proximity, one bottle of Rosa's plum wine, and truths surface in the dark. Emotional beat: intimacy she can't control.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Their Twenties
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The storm night unravels: what Beatrix abandoned, why Elias let her, and the almost-kiss that ended everything. Julian realizes he's a rival for more than the building. Emotional beat: confession as detonation.

chapters.title: Morning, Thawed
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The snow melts; nothing else does. Elias retreats into the case, Julian courts her openly, and the town takes sides over pastry counters. Emotional beat: the cost of being visible.

chapters.title: Hearing Dates and Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian files to landmark the bakery, forcing a public hearing that will drag Rosa's debts and Beatrix's testimony into daylight. Emotional beat: hope weaponized.

chapters.title: The Cello in the Attic
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Julian finds Rosa's old cello in the attic and asks her to play at the hearing. She refuses, then plays alone at midnight with shaking hands. Emotional beat: the first note back is a small resurrection.

chapters.title: Deposition
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Under deposition pressure, Beatrix admits the truth of her final performance: she froze because of a sabotage she never named. Elias realizes the case can expose it. Emotional beat: justice and betrayal wearing the same face.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. She gives Julian pieces of herself, a date, a duet rehearsal, a story, while Elias watches from across the square. Emotional beat: lending pieces of a heart to avoid risking the whole.

chapters.title: The Letter Rosa Never Sent
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In Rosa's recipe tin she finds a letter: Rosa knew about the sabotage and the man behind it, a conductor now powerful enough to bury the truth. Emotional beat: inheritance as a call to courage.

chapters.title: Crosscurrents
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers his firm's client is tied to the conductor who destroyed Beatrix. Winning the case means finishing what was done to her. Emotional beat: duty and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Offer She Should Take
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers Beatrix a clean exit: his testimony, his protection, his hand, and a life far from Merrow Point. Emotional beat: a good man offering a smaller love.

chapters.title: Burning the Recipe Book
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The bakery is vandalized the night before the hearing; Rosa's recipe book burns. Beatrix breaks, then hardens. Emotional beat: rage as the doorway out of shame.

chapters.title: What Elias Did in the Dark
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias burns his career down: he turns over evidence against his own client and the conductor, resigning mid-case. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty losing.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. In a packed town hall, she testifies, names the conductor, and, when her voice fails, picks up Rosa's cello and plays the piece that broke her, finishing it. Emotional beat: the climax, a performance completed at last.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The bakery is landmarked; the development collapses; Julian concedes gracefully, telling Beatrix he never stood a chance against a finished symphony. Emotional beat: honorable heartbreak.

chapters.title: Time Already Running Out
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A symphony offers Beatrix a principal chair in Vienna, beginning in three weeks. Elias, jobless and proud, pushes her to go. Emotional beat: the old fear of choosing love over self returns, reversed.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the summer's last market day, Elias asks for nothing, and Beatrix realizes she's done lending pieces. She asks him to come with her, or to let her come back whole. Emotional beat: the risk of the whole heart, taken.

chapters.title: A Bakery for Every Summer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Epilogue a year later: the bakery thrives under new management, Beatrix plays Vienna and returns each June, and Elias meets her train with flour on his hands. Emotional beat: love as a place you return to, not a thing you flee.
